key_insight: MolecularIQ introduces a symbolic verification framework that tests whether models truly reason over molecular graphs rather than rely on memorized chemical text; it exposes structural failures by checking model outputs against graph-derived, rule-based ground truth.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks focus on general chemical knowledge or text-based tasks and do not reliably measure a model's ability to parse and reason about the molecular graph structure that determines chemical properties.
method: Construct targeted graph-based tasks (e.g., atom/bond counting, substructure membership, stereochemistry-aware queries) that require explicit graph reasoning rather than textual recall.
Use symbolic verification: derive exact answers from molecular graphs using rule-based algorithms and compare model outputs to these unambiguous ground-truths to detect reasoning errors.
Evaluate a range of models (LLMs and graph-aware models) on these tasks to quantify chemical-graph reasoning strengths and failure modes.
impact: Provides a focused, interpretable benchmark that reveals whether AI models genuinely understand molecular structure—guiding model selection, architecture design, and targeted fine-tuning for chemistry applications.
visual_elements: Schematic molecular graph annotated with a sample query (e.g., 'number of aromatic rings') and the symbolic derivation of the answer

paper_title: MolecularIQ: Characterizing Chemical Reasoning Capabilities Through Symbolic Verification on Molecular Graphs
paper_authors: Christoph Bartmann, Johannes Schimunek, Mykyta Ielanskyi, Philipp Seidl, Günter Klambauer
